text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE STRAITS TIMES:

- Four hundred families in Singapore start checking whether computers really as amazing as they are made out to be, in trial phase of Singapore One government plan to make the country a "wired island" with each household linked to multi-media services.
- Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong arrives in Manila for start of three-day official visit to add fresh momentum to bilateral ties with Philippines.
- Senior Chinese military official expresses China's opposition to move by Japan and U.S. to expand scope of bilateral security treaty.
- Two Singaporeans seriously ill at Singapore General Hospital after developing malaria following separate trips to Bintan, a nearby Indonesian island.
- Singapore's vital electronics industry grows for first time in six months -- helping manufacturing sector record a marginal expansion.
- Malaysian finance institutions MBf Capital and Suria Capital Holdings seek government permission to begin talks on possible merger.
- Singapore Federation of Chambers of Commerce and Industry (SFCCI) will appoint full-time secretary-general next month, ending current two-yearly rotation of post among five constituent members.
THE BUSINESS TIMES:

- Property developers turning to service apartments for better returns. At least four major players -- Fraser & Neave, Kuok group, United Engineers and Wing Tai Land -- entering service apartments market for first time this year.
- World Trade Centre auditorium yesterday reverberated to pounding of drums and dances with smoke signals as major trade show Asia Telecom 97 begins.
- Surprise surge by yen against U.S. dollar and other currencies sends Tokyo stock prices tumbling on fears a further bout of instability could damage Japan's export-led economic recovery.
- It may be a telling sign of the state of the economy -- the moneylending business is growing by leaps and bounds.
- Mainboard-listed battery maker GP Batteries reports full-year unaudited net earnings rise of 14.5 percent to Singapore $23.7 million for year ended March 1997, in line with analysts' expectations.

- Creative Technology says it and US subsidiary Creative Labs Inc obtain additional preliminary injunction in lawsuit against Cyrix Corp and some OEM customers of Cyrix's Media GX chip, including Compaq.
- Hotel Properties Ltd (HPL) sells travel arm which has mostly been making losses since operations began seven years ago.
- Telekom Malaysia Bhd signs deal to take 20 percent stake in Thai-based Samart Corp plc and 33 percent stake in mobile phone subsidiary Digital Phone Co for total of US$206.6 million.
- Newly-listed Excel Machine Tools posts interim net earnings of S$3.1 million on a turnover of S$31.6 million in maiden public announcement of results for the half-year ended March.
- Telephone cord maker Huan Hsin Holdings receives lukewarm response to public tranche of eight million shares. Shares 18 times subscribed -- one of lowest take-up rates among recent new listings.
-- Singapore newsroom 65-8703080
